subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Number System, Fractions, Decimals, Basic Algebra & Geometry

notes.summary: Numbers help us count, compare, and measure quantities systematically. In this chapter, we explore Indian and International systems of numeration, place value charts, estimation rules, and Roman numerals.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Comparing Large Numbers
keyConcepts.body: When comparing two numbers, the number with more digits is always greater. If the number of digits is equal, compare the leftmost digit (highest place value) first and proceed rightwards.

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Indian vs. International System of Numeration
keyConcepts.body: In the Indian system, commas are placed after 3 digits from the right, and then every 2 digits (Ones, Thousands, Lakhs, Crores). In the International system, commas are placed every 3 digits from the right (Ones, Thousands, Millions, Billions).

keyConcepts.heading: 3. Estimation & Rounding Off
keyConcepts.body: To round off to the nearest ten, inspect the ones digit (if 5 or more, round up; otherwise round down). Apply the same principle for rounding to nearest hundred and thousand.

formulas: 1 Lakh = 100 Thousands = 1,00,000
1 Crore = 100 Lakhs = 10 Millions = 1,00,00,000
1 Million = 10 Lakhs = 1,000,000
Roman Numerals: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1000

objectiveQuestions.question: How many lakhs make 1 billion in the Indian system of numeration?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: 1 Billion = 1,000,000,000 (9 zeros). Since 1 Lakh = 1,00,000 (5 zeros), 1 Billion / 1 Lakh = 10,000 Lakhs.

objectiveQuestions.question: What is the predecessor of the smallest 6-digit number?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The smallest 6-digit number is 1,00,000. Its predecessor is 1,00,000 - 1 = 99,999 (largest 5-digit number).

subjectiveQuestions.question: Insert commas suitably and write the number name of 87595762 in both Indian and International Systems of Numeration.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Indian System: 8,75,95,762 — Eight crore seventy-five lakh ninety-five thousand seven hundred sixty-two.

International System: 87,595,762 — Eighty-seven million five hundred ninety-five thousand seven hundred sixty-two.

subjectiveQuestions.question: A book exhibition was held for four days in a school. The number of tickets sold at the counter on the first, second, third, and final day was respectively 1094, 1812, 2050, and 2751. Find the total number of tickets sold on all the four days.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Step 1: Write down tickets sold on each day:
• Day 1 = 1,094
• Day 2 = 1,812
• Day 3 = 2,050
• Day 4 = 2,751

Step 2: Add all four values together:
Total tickets sold = 1094 + 1812 + 2050 + 2751 = 7,707 tickets.

Conclusion: A total of 7,707 tickets were sold across all four days of the exhibition.

subjects.name: Science
subjects.description: Components of Food, Sorting Materials, Living Organisms, Light & Magnets

notes.summary: Our food contains essential chemical substances called nutrients: Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, Vitamins, and Minerals, along with dietary fibres (roughage) and water.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Energy-Giving vs. Body-Building Nutrients
keyConcepts.body: Carbohydrates and Fats provide energy to our body (fats give more than double the energy per gram compared to carbohydrates). Proteins are required for growth and tissue repair, so they are called body-building foods.

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Biochemical Tests for Nutrients
keyConcepts.body: Starch test: Add 2–3 drops of dilute iodine solution; a blue-black colour confirms starch. Protein test: Add 2 drops of copper sulphate solution and 10 drops of caustic soda; a violet colour confirms protein.

formulas: Starch + Dilute Iodine Solution → Blue-Black Colour
Protein + CuSO4 (2 drops) + NaOH (10 drops) → Violet Colour
Vitamin D Deficiency → Rickets | Iron Deficiency → Anaemia

objectiveQuestions.question: Which reagent turns blue-black in the presence of starch?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Dilute iodine solution reacts with amylose in starch to produce a characteristic deep blue-black colour.

subjectiveQuestions.question: What are deficiency diseases? Name any three vitamin deficiency diseases along with their symptoms.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Diseases that occur due to the lack of specific nutrients over a long period are called deficiency diseases.
1. Vitamin A — Loss of vision / Night blindness (poor vision in dim light).
2. Vitamin B1 — Beriberi (weak muscles and very little energy to work).
3. Vitamin C — Scurvy (bleeding gums and wounds taking longer time to heal).

subjects.name: Science
subjects.description: Nutrition in Plants & Animals, Heat, Acids Bases & Salts, Electric Current

notes.summary: Green plants synthesize their own food via photosynthesis using chlorophyll, sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide. Non-green plants and fungi rely on heterotrophic modes like parasitic, saprotrophic, or symbiotic nutrition.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Photosynthesis Process
keyConcepts.body: Leaves are the food factories of plants. Stomata surrounded by guard cells regulate gas exchange, while xylem vessels transport water and minerals from roots to leaves.

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Symbiotic Relationship & Nitrogen Fixation
keyConcepts.body: Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of leguminous plants (gram, peas, moong) and convert atmospheric nitrogen into soluble nitrates in exchange for shelter and food.

formulas: 6CO2 + 6H2O —(Sunlight / Chlorophyll)→ C6H12O6 (Glucose) + 6O2
Lichens = Symbiosis between Algae (prepares food) + Fungus (provides shelter & water)

objectiveQuestions.question: Cuscuta (Amarbel) is an example of:
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Cuscuta lacks chlorophyll and derives ready-made nutrients directly from the host plant on which it climbs, making it a total stem parasite.

subjectiveQuestions.question: Why do farmers grow leguminous crops alternatively with cereal crops?
subjectiveQuestions.solution: Leguminous crops (like pulses, peas, and beans) harbour Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules. These bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into soluble nitrogenous compounds in the soil, naturally replenishing soil fertility and reducing the need for chemical urea fertilizers.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Rational Numbers, Linear Equations, Quadrilaterals, Mensuration & Algebraic Identities

notes.summary: A rational number is any number that can be expressed in the form p/q where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. Between any two given rational numbers, there exist infinitely many rational numbers.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Multiplicative Inverse (Reciprocal)
keyConcepts.body: If p/q is a non-zero rational number, its multiplicative inverse is q/p such that (p/q) × (q/p) = 1. Zero has no reciprocal.

formulas: Mean Method: A rational number between a and b is (a + b) / 2
Distributivity: a(b - c) = ab - ac

objectiveQuestions.question: Which rational number does NOT have a reciprocal?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Division by zero is undefined (1/0 is undefined), so 0 does not have a multiplicative inverse (reciprocal).

subjectiveQuestions.question: Find five rational numbers between 2/3 and 4/5.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Step 1: Convert both fractions to a common denominator (LCM of 3 and 5 is 15):
2/3 = 10/15 and 4/5 = 12/15.
Step 2: Multiply numerator and denominator by 4 to create sufficient gap:
10/15 = 40/60 and 12/15 = 48/60.
Step 3: Five rational numbers between 40/60 and 48/60 are:
41/60, 42/60, 43/60, 44/60, and 45/60.

subjects.name: Science (Physics, Chem, Bio)
subjects.description: Motion, Laws of Motion, Gravitation, Matter, Atoms & Molecules, The Fundamental Unit of Life

notes.summary: Motion is the change in position of an object with respect to time and a reference point. We distinguish between scalar quantities (distance, speed) and vector quantities (displacement, velocity, acceleration) and derive the three equations of uniformly accelerated motion.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Distance vs. Displacement
keyConcepts.body: Distance is the actual path length travelled by an object (always positive, scalar). Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from initial to final position along with direction (can be positive, negative, or zero, vector).

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Graphical Representation of Motion
keyConcepts.body: The slope of a Displacement-Time (s-t) graph gives velocity. The slope of a Velocity-Time (v-t) graph gives acceleration, and the area enclosed under a v-t graph gives the total displacement.

formulas: First Equation of Motion: v = u + at
Second Equation of Motion: s = ut + ½at²
Third Equation of Motion: v² - u² = 2as
Uniform Circular Motion Speed: v = 2πr / t

objectiveQuestions.question: What does the area under a Velocity-Time (v-t) graph represent?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Since Displacement = Velocity × Time, the geometric area enclosed under a Velocity-Time graph gives the magnitude of displacement for that time interval.

objectiveQuestions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from 18 km/h to 36 km/h in 5 seconds. What is its acceleration in m/s²?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Convert speeds to m/s: u = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s; v = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s. Using a = (v - u)/t = (10 - 5)/5 = 1 m/s².

subjectiveQuestions.question: Distinguish between uniform velocity and uniform acceleration. Can a body have zero velocity and still have non-zero acceleration? Give an example.
subjectiveQuestions.solution: Yes! When a ball is thrown vertically upwards, at the highest point of its trajectory its instantaneous velocity becomes zero (v = 0), but it continues to experience a constant downward acceleration due to gravity (g = 9.8 m/s²).

subjectiveQuestions.question: Derive the second equation of motion s = ut + ½at² graphically using a Velocity-Time graph.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Consider a body moving with initial velocity 'u' at t = 0 and reaching final velocity 'v' at time 't' with uniform acceleration 'a'.

1. On the v-t graph, let OA = u, BC = v, and OC = t.
2. The distance 's' travelled in time 't' equals the area of trapezium OABC under the line AB.
3. Area of trapezium OABC = Area of rectangle OADC + Area of triangle ABD
   s = (OA × OC) + ½ × (AD × BD)
4. Substitute OA = u, OC = AD = t, and BD = (v - u) = at (from v = u + at):
   s = (u × t) + ½ × (t × at)
   s = ut + ½at².
Hence proved.

subjects.name: Science
subjects.description: Chemical Reactions, Acids & Bases, Life Processes, Light Reflection & Refraction, Electricity

notes.summary: A chemical reaction involves the breaking and making of bonds between atoms to produce new substances with distinct properties. According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, every chemical equation must have an equal number of atoms of each element on both the reactant and product sides.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Five Core Types of Chemical Reactions
keyConcepts.body:
• Combination Reaction: Two or more reactants combine to form a single product (e.g., burning of coal, slaking of lime).
• Decomposition Reaction: A single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products via heat (thermal), light (photolytic), or electricity (electrolytic).
• Displacement Reaction: A more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its salt solution.
• Double Displacement (Precipitation): Exchange of ions between two aqueous reactants.
• Redox Reaction: Simultaneous oxidation (gain of O / loss of H) and reduction (loss of O / gain of H).

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Exothermic vs. Endothermic Processes
keyConcepts.body: Reactions that release heat energy along with products (such as respiration, combustion of natural gas, and slaking of quicklime) are exothermic. Reactions that absorb energy are endothermic.

keyConcepts.heading: 3. Corrosion and Rancidity in Everyday Life
keyConcepts.body: Corrosion is the slow degradation of metals by moisture and atmospheric gases (rusting of iron, black coating of Ag2S on silver, green basic copper carbonate on copper). Rancidity is the aerial oxidation of fats and oils, prevented by flushing nitrogen gas in chips packets.

formulas: Slaking of Lime: CaO(s) [Quicklime] + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq) [Slaked Lime] + Heat
Whitewashing Shine: Ca(OH)2(aq) + CO2(g) → CaCO3(s) [Marble finish] + H2O(l)
Thermal Decomposition of Ferrous Sulphate: 2FeSO4(s) —(Heat)→ Fe2O3(s) + SO2(g) + SO3(g)
Photolytic Decomposition (Black & White Photography): 2AgBr(s) —(Sunlight)→ 2Ag(s) + Br2(g)

objectiveQuestions.question: Before burning in air, the magnesium ribbon is cleaned by rubbing with sandpaper to:
options: Make the ribbon surface shiny for better reflection
Remove the protective layer of basic magnesium carbonate / magnesium oxide
Remove moisture absorbed from the atmosphere
Convert metallic magnesium into magnesium nitride
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Magnesium is a reactive metal that forms a slow passive layer of magnesium oxide / basic magnesium carbonate when exposed to air, which hinders smooth combustion.

objectiveQuestions.question: During the electrolysis of water (2H2O → 2H2 + O2), the mole and volume ratio of Hydrogen gas to Oxygen gas collected at the electrodes is:
objectiveQuestions.explanation: 2 moles of H2O decompose to yield 2 volumes of Hydrogen gas at the cathode and 1 volume of Oxygen gas at the anode, giving a 2 : 1 volume ratio.

objectiveQuestions.question: When lead nitrate powder is heated strongly in a dry boiling tube, brown fumes are evolved. These brown fumes are of:
objectiveQuestions.explanation: 2Pb(NO3)2(s) —(Heat)→ 2PbO(s) [Yellow residue] + 4NO2(g) [Brown fumes] + O2(g).

objectiveQuestions.question: In the reaction CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O, which substance acts as the reducing agent?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: H2 gains oxygen to become H2O (it is oxidized) and removes oxygen from CuO, so H2 is the reducing agent.

subjectiveQuestions.question: Why are potato chips bags flushed with Nitrogen gas by manufacturers?
subjectiveQuestions.solution: Oil and fat-containing food items undergo aerial oxidation when exposed to oxygen, turning rancid with a foul smell and taste. Nitrogen is an unreactive (inert) gas at room temperature; flushing bags with nitrogen displaces oxygen and prevents rancidity, keeping chips crisp and fresh.

subjectiveQuestions.question: Why does the blue colour of copper sulphate solution fade and turn pale green when an iron nail is dipped in it for 20 minutes?
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Iron (Fe) lies higher than Copper (Cu) in the reactivity series of metals. When an iron nail is immersed in aqueous blue copper sulphate (CuSO4), iron displaces copper from its salt solution:

Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) [Blue] → FeSO4(aq) [Pale Green] + Cu(s) [Reddish-Brown deposit]

Consequently, a reddish-brown coating of metallic copper deposits on the iron nail and the solution turns pale green due to the formation of ferrous sulphate (FeSO4).

subjectiveQuestions.question: What is a decomposition reaction? Explain Thermal, Electrolytic, and Photolytic decomposition reactions with one balanced chemical equation for each.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
A reaction in which a single compound splits into two or more simpler substances under suitable energy conditions is called a decomposition reaction.

1. Thermal Decomposition (Carried out by Heat):
When calcium carbonate (limestone) is strongly heated, it decomposes into calcium oxide (quicklime) and carbon dioxide:
CaCO3(s) —(Heat)→ CaO(s) + CO2(g)

2. Electrolytic Decomposition (Carried out by Electric Current):
When electric current is passed through acidified water, it decomposes into hydrogen and oxygen gas:
2H2O(l) —(Electric Current)→ 2H2(g) [Cathode] + O2(g) [Anode]

3. Photolytic Decomposition (Carried out by Sunlight):
Silver chloride turns grey when exposed to sunlight because it decomposes into metallic silver and chlorine gas:
2AgCl(s) [White] —(Sunlight)→ 2Ag(s) [Grey] + Cl2(g)

notes.summary: Light travels in straight lines and exhibits both reflection at polished surfaces (spherical mirrors) and refraction when passing obliquely between media of different optical densities (spherical lenses).

keyConcepts.heading: 1. New Cartesian Sign Convention
keyConcepts.body: All distances are measured from the Pole (P) of the mirror or Optical Centre (O) of the lens. Distances in the direction of incident light are taken as positive (+), and those opposite are negative (-). Therefore, focal length of a concave mirror/lens is negative (-), whereas for a convex mirror/lens it is positive (+).

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Snell's Law & Refractive Index
keyConcepts.body: The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media: sin(i)/sin(r) = n21. Absolute refractive index n = c / v.

formulas: Mirror Formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f  (where f = R/2)
Lens Formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f
Magnification (Mirror): m = h'/h = -v/u | Magnification (Lens): m = h'/h = +v/u
Power of a Lens: P = 1 / f(in metres) = 100 / f(in cm) [Unit: Dioptre (D)]

objectiveQuestions.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a convex lens to obtain a real, inverted image of the same size as the object?
options: Between optical centre O and F1
objectiveQuestions.explanation: When an object is placed at 2F1 of a convex lens, a real, inverted, and same-sized image (m = -1) is formed at 2F2 on the other side.

objectiveQuestions.question: A doctor has prescribed a corrective lens of power +2.5 D. What is the focal length and nature of the lens?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: f = 100 / P = 100 / (+2.5) = +40 cm. Positive focal length indicates a converging (convex) lens.

subjectiveQuestions.question: Why are convex mirrors preferred as rear-view wing mirrors in vehicles?
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Convex mirrors are preferred as rear-view mirrors because:
1. They always produce an erect (upright), virtual, and diminished image regardless of the distance of the approaching vehicle.
2. Being curved outwards, they provide a much wider field of view than a plane mirror of the same size, enabling the driver to monitor traffic across multiple lanes.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Real Numbers, Polynomials, Quadratic Equations, Arithmetic Progressions, Trigonometry, Statistics

notes.summary: Trigonometry studies the relationship between the acute angles and side ratios of a right-angled triangle. Mastering standard angle values (0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°) and the three Pythagorean identities is key to scoring full marks in Board Exams.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Six Trigonometric Ratios
keyConcepts.body: For an acute angle θ in a right-angled triangle: sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse, tan θ = Perpendicular / Base = sin θ / cos θ. Their reciprocals are cosec θ, sec θ, and cot θ.

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Three Fundamental Pythagorean Identities
keyConcepts.body:
1) sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
2) 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ (for 0° ≤ θ < 90°)
3) 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ (for 0° < θ ≤ 90°)

formulas: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1  ⇒  sin²θ = 1 - cos²θ
sec²θ - tan²θ = 1  ⇒  (sec θ - tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = 1
cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1

objectiveQuestions.question: If sin A = 3/5, where A is an acute angle, what is the value of tan A?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: By Pythagoras Theorem, Base = √(5² - 3²) = √(25 - 9) = 4. Therefore, tan A = Perpendicular / Base = 3/4.

objectiveQuestions.question: The value of 9 sec²A - 9 tan²A is equal to:
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Factoring out 9 gives 9(sec²A - tan²A). Since sec²A - tan²A = 1, the expression equals 9 × 1 = 9.

subjectiveQuestions.question: Prove the identity: √((1 + sin A) / (1 - sin A)) = sec A + tan A.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Step 1: Take LHS = √((1 + sin A) / (1 - sin A))

Step 2: Multiply numerator and denominator inside the square root by the conjugate (1 + sin A):
LHS = √(((1 + sin A)(1 + sin A)) / ((1 - sin A)(1 + sin A)))
LHS = √((1 + sin A)² / (1 - sin²A))

Step 3: Use the identity 1 - sin²A = cos²A:
LHS = √((1 + sin A)² / cos²A)
LHS = (1 + sin A) / cos A

Step 4: Split into two terms:
LHS = (1 / cos A) + (sin A / cos A) = sec A + tan A = RHS.
Hence Proved.

subjects.name: Social Science
subjects.description: History (Nationalism in Europe & India), Geography, Political Science & Economics

notes.summary: Indian nationalism grew through shared anti-colonial struggles led by Mahatma Gandhi, notably the Satyagraha movements (Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad), the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement (1920–22), and the Civil Disobedience Movement sparked by the historic Dandi Salt March (1930).

keyConcepts.heading: 1. The Idea of Satyagraha
keyConcepts.body: Satyagraha emphasized the power of truth and non-violent resistance. Mahatma Gandhi organized successful Satyagrahas in Champaran in Bihar (1917, against oppressive indigo plantation system), Kheda in Gujarat (1917, peasant revenue relaxation), and Ahmedabad (1918, cotton mill workers).

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Rowlatt Act (1919) & Jallianwala Bagh
keyConcepts.body: The Imperial Legislative Council passed the Rowlatt Act allowing detention of political prisoners without trial for two years. On 13 April 1919, General Dyer opened fire on a peaceful Baisakhi gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar.

formulas: 1917: Champaran Satyagraha (Bihar) & Kheda Satyagraha
13 April 1919: Jallianwala Bagh Incident | Dec 1920: Nagpur Session adopts Non-Cooperation
12 March – 6 April 1930: Dandi Salt March (240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi)
Sept 1932: Poona Pact signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar

objectiveQuestions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi travel to Champaran in Bihar to inspire peasants to struggle against the oppressive plantation system?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi went to Champaran in Bihar to support indigo farmers against the oppressive Tinkathia plantation system.

subjectiveQuestions.question: Why did Mahatma Gandhi choose 'Salt' as a powerful symbol to unite the nation during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
1. Universal Essential Commodity: Salt was consumed equally by both the rich and the poor, making it an everyday necessity across all caste, class, and religious lines.
2. Unjust Colonial Monopoly: The British government imposed a heavy tax on salt and held a strict monopoly over its manufacture, which Mahatma Gandhi declared revealed the most oppressive face of British rule.
3. Mass Mobilization: On 12 March 1930, Gandhi walked 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal town of Dandi with 78 trusted volunteers, ceremonially boiling seawater on 6 April 1930 to launch the Civil Disobedience Movement nationwide.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units & Measurements, Kinematics, Laws of Motion, Work Energy & Power, Thermodynamics

notes.summary: Dimensional analysis expresses any derived physical quantity in terms of the seven fundamental SI base quantities [M, L, T, A, K, mol, cd] and checks dimensional consistency of physical equations via the Principle of Homogeneity.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Principle of Homogeneity of Dimensions
keyConcepts.body: Only physical quantities having identical dimensions can be added, subtracted, or equated. If X = A + BC, then [X] = [A] = [BC].

formulas: Force: [M¹ L¹ T⁻²] | Work / Energy / Torque: [M¹ L² T⁻²]
Universal Gravitational Constant (G): [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]
Planck's Constant (h): [M¹ L² T⁻¹] (Same as Angular Momentum)

objectiveQuestions.question: Which pair of physical quantities has identical dimensional formulas?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Impulse (F × Δt) and Linear Momentum (m × v) both have the dimensional formula [M¹ L¹ T⁻¹].

subjectiveQuestions.question: In the van der Waals equation (P + a/V²)(V - b) = RT, find the dimensions of constants 'a' and 'b'.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
By the Principle of Homogeneity:
1. Since 'b' is subtracted from volume V, [b] = [V] = [M⁰ L³ T⁰].
2. Since a/V² is added to pressure P, [a / V²] = [P]
   ⇒ [a] = [P] × [V²] = [M¹ L⁻¹ T⁻²] × [L⁶] = [M¹ L⁵ T⁻²].

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electrostatics, Current Electricity, Magnetism, Optics, Dual Nature & Semiconductors

notes.summary: Electrostatics deals with forces, fields, and potentials arising from stationary electric charges. Key board derivations include Electric Field on Axial and Equatorial lines of an Electric Dipole and applications of Gauss's Law.

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Quantization & Conservation of Charge
keyConcepts.body: Total charge on any body is always an integral multiple of the basic elementary charge: q = ±ne, where e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

keyConcepts.heading: 2. Gauss's Law in Electrostatics
keyConcepts.body: The total electric flux Φ_E through any closed Gaussian surface in free space is equal to 1/ε₀ times the net electric charge enclosed within the surface: Φ_E = ∮ E · dA = q_enclosed / ε₀.

formulas: Coulomb's Law: F = (1 / 4πε₀) · (|q₁q₂| / r²)  where 1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²
Dipole Axial Field: E_axial = (1 / 4πε₀) · (2p / r³) | Equatorial: E_eq = (1 / 4πε₀) · (p / r³)
Torque on Dipole in Uniform Field: τ = p × E = pE sin θ
Gauss's Law: Φ_E = q_enclosed / ε₀

objectiveQuestions.question: For a short electric dipole, the ratio of electric field intensity at a point on the axial line to a point at the same distance on the equatorial line is:
objectiveQuestions.explanation: For a short dipole (r >> a), E_axial = 2kp/r³ and E_equatorial = kp/r³. Therefore, E_axial : E_equatorial = 2 : 1.

objectiveQuestions.question: An electric dipole of dipole moment p is placed inside a closed cube of side L. What is the net electric flux emerging through the cube?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: An electric dipole consists of two equal and opposite charges (+q and -q), so the net enclosed charge q_enclosed = +q - q = 0. By Gauss's Law, Φ = 0.

subjectiveQuestions.question: Why can two electrostatic field lines never intersect each other?
subjectiveQuestions.solution: The tangent drawn at any point on an electric field line gives the direction of the net electric field intensity at that point. If two field lines intersected, there would be two tangents—and hence two distinct directions of the net electric field—at the single point of intersection, which is physically impossible.

subjectiveQuestions.question: State Gauss's Law in electrostatics. Using this law, derive an expression for the electric field due to an infinitely long straight uniformly charged wire of linear charge density λ.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Statement: The total electric flux through any closed surface in free space is 1/ε₀ times the net charge enclosed by that surface: Φ_E = ∮ E · dS = q_in / ε₀.

Derivation:
1. Consider an infinitely long thin straight wire with uniform linear charge density λ (charge per unit length).
2. By symmetry, the electric field E points radially outward and has the same magnitude at all points at radial distance 'r'.
3. Construct a coaxial cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius 'r' and length 'l'.
4. For the two flat circular caps, E is perpendicular to dS (θ = 90°), so flux through caps = 0.
5. For the curved cylindrical surface, E is parallel to dS (θ = 0°):
   Φ_E = E × (Area of curved surface) = E × (2πrl).
6. Charge enclosed inside cylinder: q_in = λl.
7. Applying Gauss's Law:
   E(2πrl) = λl / ε₀  ⇒  E = λ / (2πrε₀).
Hence derived.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Relations & Functions, Matrices, Determinants, Continuity & Differentiability, Integrals, Vectors

notes.summary: A real function f is continuous at x = c if Left Hand Limit (LHL) = Right Hand Limit (RHL) = f(c). Every differentiable function is continuous, though the converse is not necessarily true (e.g., f(x) = |x| at x = 0).

keyConcepts.heading: 1. Chain Rule & Logarithmic Differentiation
keyConcepts.body: For composite functions y = f(g(x)), dy/dx = f'(g(x)) · g'(x). For functions of the form y = [u(x)]^[v(x)], take natural logarithm (ln) on both sides before differentiating.

formulas: Continuity at x = c: lim(x→c⁻) f(x) = lim(x→c⁺) f(x) = f(c)
d/dx (sin⁻¹x) = 1 / √(1 - x²) | d/dx (tan⁻¹x) = 1 / (1 + x²)
d/dx (e^x) = e^x | d/dx (ln x) = 1/x

objectiveQuestions.question: If y = log(sin(e^x)), then dy/dx is equal to:
objectiveQuestions.explanation: By the Chain Rule: dy/dx = (1 / sin(e^x)) · cos(e^x) · e^x = e^x cot(e^x).

subjectiveQuestions.question: If y = x^x, find dy/dx using logarithmic differentiation.
subjectiveQuestions.solution:
Step 1: Given y = x^x (for x > 0).
Step 2: Take natural logarithm (log_e) on both sides:
log y = log(x^x) = x · log x
Step 3: Differentiate both sides with respect to x using the Product Rule:
(1/y) · (dy/dx) = x · (1/x) + (log x) · 1
(1/y) · (dy/dx) = 1 + log x
Step 4: Multiply both sides by y = x^x:
dy/dx = x^x (1 + log x).

mockTests.title: Class 10 Science — Full Board Pattern Mock Test
mockTests.subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry & Biology)

questions.question: Which of the following reactions represents an endothermic process?
options: Burning of natural gas (methane) in air
Dilution of concentrated sulphuric acid with water
questions.explanation: Decomposition of limestone (CaCO3 → CaO + CO2) requires continuous absorption of heat energy, making it an endothermic reaction.

questions.question: An object is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Where will the image be formed?
options: At 20 cm in front of the mirror (at Centre of Curvature C)
Between Focus F and Pole P
questions.explanation: Since f = 10 cm, the Centre of Curvature C is at R = 2f = 20 cm. An object at C forms a real, inverted, same-sized image right at C (20 cm in front of the mirror).

questions.question: In human beings, the breakdown of pyruvate to give carbon dioxide, water, and abundant ATP energy takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Aerobic breakdown of 3-carbon pyruvate into CO2, H2O, and 38 ATP molecules via the Krebs cycle takes place inside the Mitochondria.

questions.question: If the length of a cylindrical metallic wire is doubled by stretching it while keeping its volume constant, its electrical resistance becomes:
questions.explanation: When stretched at constant volume, doubling length (L' = 2L) halves the cross-sectional area (A' = A/2). Thus R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4(ρL/A) = 4R.

questions.question: An aqueous solution turns red litmus solution blue. Excess addition of which of the following solutions would reverse the change?
questions.explanation: Turning red litmus blue indicates a basic solution. Adding excess Hydrochloric acid (HCl) neutralizes the base and makes the medium acidic, turning blue litmus back to red.

mockTests.title: Class 12 Physics & Maths — High-Yield Board Booster
mockTests.subject: Physics & Mathematics

questions.question: The SI unit of electric flux (Φ_E) is:
questions.explanation: Electric flux Φ_E = E · A has units (N/C)·m² = N·m²/C, which is also equivalent to (V/m)·m = Volt·metre (V·m).

questions.question: If A is a square matrix of order 3 × 3 such that |A| = 5, then the value of |adj(A)| is:
questions.explanation: For a square matrix A of order n, |adj(A)| = |A|^(n-1). Here n = 3 and |A| = 5, so |adj(A)| = 5^(3-1) = 5² = 25.

questions.question: Kirchhoff's First Law (Junction Rule, ΣI = 0) at an electrical junction is based on the law of conservation of:
questions.explanation: Kirchhoff's Current Law (Junction Rule) states that total current entering a junction equals total current leaving it, which follows from the conservation of electric charge.

questions.question: The derivative of sin⁻¹(x) + cos⁻¹(x) with respect to x (for x ∈ [-1, 1]) is:
questions.explanation: Since sin⁻¹(x) + cos⁻¹(x) = π/2 (a constant) for all x ∈ [-1, 1], its derivative with respect to x is 0.

questions.question: When monochromatic light passes from air into a glass slab of refractive index 1.5, which quantity remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: Frequency is an intrinsic property of the source of light and remains invariant during refraction from one medium to another.
